questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature in Switzerland and the possibility of improving my german. And to experience a different health care system than the danish one.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The exchange office in Zurich sent out most of the documents (and other practical information) you needed upon arrival. That was very helpful. They also have orientation-nights where they tell you a lot of good, practical information regarding your stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The exchange office in Zurich were extremely kind and fast at replying if you had a question, so they are a fantastic help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me because I was offered housing through the university. But I've heard from other students that it can be a little difficult if you don't get offered anything from the school.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy to get around with public transport in Zurich, so living off campus is not at problem.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It can be a little tricky to keep track of all the things you need to do when registrating. But again, the exchange office is very helpful in that proces and are there to answer all questions you may have. They also tell you, what you need to be aware of, and what type of information they need from you. That makes it a lot easier to navigate in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange-coordinator has an e-mail, which they respond very quickly to. And if you really have a problem, they may call you or offer, that you can call them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. I had to send my wishes to the exchange-coordinator, and then she booked the classes for me. That's how it works with medical exchange but from what I've heard not other study-areas.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of deadlines and start the process in advance, so you don't end up in a last-minute-situation!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was the same as the level af UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was the same but they do have more lectures, than what I'm used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Clinical courses: Pediatrics, radiology, nuclear medicine, pathology
Elective module: Public Health
Lectures: dermatology, forensic medicine, pediatrics, general medicine, hematology, kidney diseases, anaesthesiology, emergency medicine

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the clinical course in Pediatrics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay for some mandatory things for instance your residence permit.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was actually pretty much how I expected it. The prices are a little higher than the danish prices but not as high or different as I thought they would be.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They have free gym at the different campuses, with a lot of different options, both gym-classes and "normal" gyms. 
Furthermore, they have numerous cafeterias and different student bars.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the gym! They are very nice!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Experience the nature!! It's absolutely amazing. If you're under 25 (and four people travelling together) they offer a "Friends-pass" with the train, which makes even longer trips very cheap. I can for sure recommend that!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: That was very easy. The culture in Switzerland is pretty similar to the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students are very nice, but you often have to be the one taking the first step. But when you do, you'll experience that they are quite friendly!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't experience challenging cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That being active (skiing, hiking etc.) is a big part of the swiss culture. I really loved that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-Keep track of the things (beside registration at the university) that you have to do (like getting a residence permit etc.). Especially in the beginning there are different practical things, you have to do.

-They offer german courses in the beginning of the semester. I would sign up for one. It gives you a chance to adapt to hearing german on a daily basis, and you get the chance to meet other students, that signed up as well. 

-Be openminded and smile - then you'll have an amazing time!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Say yes if they offer you student housing. It may not be luxury, but it takes away some stress regarding finding a home and also gives you an opportunity to meet other students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met during my exchange. The experience would not have been the same without them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: They teach in german, so in the beginning you'll need some time to adapt to that. But after a short period of time you don't pay attention to it anymore - and you really end up improving your german skills!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
